question: A can do a work in 10 days and B can do the same work in 20 days. If they work on it together for 6 days, then what fraction of the work is left?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work = LCM(10, 20) = 20 units.

Combined efficiency of A and B = 2 + 1 = 3 units/day.

Work done in 6 days = 6 × 3 = 18 units.

Fraction of work done = 18 ÷ 20 = 9/10.

Remaining work = 1 − 9/10 = 1/10.

**∴ The correct answer is 1/10.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by A = 10 days

Time taken by B = 20 days

Number of days worked together = 6 days

**Calculations:**

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 A
 10
 20
 2
 
 

 B
 20
 1
 
 

⇒ Total efficiency of A and B = 2 + 1 = 3 units/day.

⇒ Work done by A and B together in 6 days = 6 × 3 = 18 units.

⇒ Remaining work = Total work − Work done = 20 − 18 = 2 units.

⇒ Fraction of work left = Remaining work ÷ Total work

⇒ Fraction of work left = 2 ÷ 20 = 1/10.

**∴ The correct answer is 1/10.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes & Cisterns

This concept follows the same LCM efficiency logic as Time & Work, where an inlet pipe does positive work (+ efficiency) and an outlet pipe does negative work (− efficiency).

Work & Wages

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the actual work done by each individual. If they work for the same duration, wages are distributed in the ratio of their efficiencies.

Alternate Day Work

When individuals work on alternate days, find the work done in a complete cycle (e.g., 2 days) and then multiply to get as close to total work as possible before adding the remaining work individually.
